title: Reconstruction of a normalized tower
statement:
Let $C_\bullet\in\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)$ be normalized
([sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]). Then $R\varprojlim_n C_n$ lies in
$\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$, and for every $m$ the natural map

$$
\bigl(R\varprojlim_n C_n\bigr)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_{E,T}}
\mathcal O_{E,T}/\ell^m\longrightarrow C_m
$$

is an isomorphism in $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^m)$.

proof.text: Put $O=\mathcal O_E$, $R=\mathcal O_{E,T}$ and $B_n=(O/\ell^n)_T$. The current coefficient-tower definition identifies $R$ canonically with $\varprojlim_n B_n$, compatibly with the finite projections; we use this identification, so that $B_n$ retains the definition's constant finite-ring meaning. Choose a uniformizer $\pi$ of $O$. The DVR statement gives $\ell=u\pi^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$: the valuation is positive since the absolute value extends the $\ell$-adic one. Thus $O$ is Noetherian (every ideal is principal), and $(\ell^n)$ and $(\pi^j)$ are cofinal. We keep the given $\ell$-tower; we do not identify $\ell$ with $\pi$. Apply constant-completion flatness and its quotient assertion with $A=O,I=(\ell)$. This identifies $R/\ell^nR=B_n$ and makes multiplication by $\ell^m$ injective on $R$: tensor the injective map $\underline O\xrightarrow{\ell^m}\underline O$ with the flat $R$. Hence $K_m=[R\xrightarrow{\ell^m}R]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ resolves $B_m$. The analogous assertion holds for $[R\xrightarrow{\pi^j}R]$ using $I=(\pi)$ and the cofinal identification of completions from the coefficient definition. These two-term complexes are K-flat: tensoring one with an acyclic complex gives a shifted mapping cone of a scalar map between acyclic complexes, which is acyclic by the long exact cohomology sequence. Each quotient $O/\pi^s$ is finite: its filtration by powers of $\pi$ has $s$ successive factors $\pi^iO/\pi^{i+1}O\cong O/\pi$, by multiplication by $\pi^i$ and cancellation in the domain $O$, and the DVR statement gives a finite residue field. In particular $O/\ell^n=O/\pi^{en}$ is finite.

source.place: Coefficient setup and the sentence that reduction is the cone of multiplication; Bhatt–Scholze §3.5; Stacks Tags 093M, 099M

proof.text: Read normalization in its current derived coefficient-tower sense: $C_\bullet$ is an object of $D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,O))$ and each $C_n$ is an object of $D(B_n)$. Choose integers $a\leq b$ containing the cohomological and Tor amplitudes of every $C_n$, as supplied by that definition, enlarging the two common intervals to one if necessary. For every $1\leq m\leq n$ it asserts that the canonical transition-induced map $C_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m\to C_m$ is an isomorphism in $D(B_m)$; no normalization over $R$ is assumed. Restricting scalars level by level gives a strict $R$-tower in the derived category of strict inverse sequences. Evaluation is exact, so its evaluations are precisely the given $C_n$. To compute with finite-coefficient complexes, choose a K-flat $B_1$-complex $Q_1$ representing $C_1$. Inductively, in $D(B_{n+1})$ represent the transition $C_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}Q_n$ by a roof with a quasi-isomorphism on its left leg; resolve the roof's middle complex by a K-flat complex $Q_{n+1}$ with flat terms. Composing its map to the right leg gives a strict semilinear chain map $Q_{n+1}\to Q_n$. Longer transitions are their composites. At each induction stage the left roof leg and the resolution give an isomorphism $Q_n\simeq C_n$ in $D(B_n)$, and the constructed transition represents the given transition in $D(B_{n+1})$ after restricting the target along $B_{n+1}\to B_n$. Consequently the isomorphisms are compatible also after restriction to $D(R)$. We retain these particular finite-coefficient isomorphisms when checking normalization in step 5. The sequential evaluation-fullness statement lifts this compatible family to an isomorphism of strict $R$-towers in their derived category. It asserts existence, not uniqueness: fix one lift. It preserves each evaluation and transition and hence the projections from its derived limit. We may compute $C=R\lim_n C_n$ on this $Q$-tower.

source.place: Realize the given coherent tower before the coefficient-fiber calculation; Stacks Tags 05RT, 06YS, 0940–0941

proof.text: The repleteness statement for every scheme is [det-pe-replete-epimorphism]. Here is its exact-products consequence used by the unit. Given a countable family of epimorphisms $M_i\to N_i$ of module sheaves, put $E_r=(\prod_{i\leq r}M_i)\times(\prod_{i>r}N_i)$ for $r\geq0$, with transition replacing the $(r+1)$st $M$ coordinate by its image in $N$. Each transition is epimorphic: lifting its one new coordinate is a local lifting problem for the given epimorphism. The inverse limit is $\prod_i M_i$, since each coordinate eventually is its $M_i$ coordinate; its projection to $E_0=\prod_i N_i$ is precisely $\prod_i(M_i\to N_i)$. Repleteness makes this projection epimorphic. Products preserve kernels by their coordinate universal property, so countable module products are exact. The existing countable-products statement also identifies them sectionwise for the coefficient sheaf $R$. Consequently derived products here are termwise products and commute with cohomology. The strict-tower limit has the natural Roos model $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod Q_n\to\prod Q_n)[-1]$. For fixed $m$, deleting the finite prefix $n<m$ does not change this model up to quasi-isomorphism, compatibly with all remaining projections. Indeed, write each product as its finite prefix plus tail. On the prefix the operator $1-s$ is an upper triangular finite matrix with identity diagonal; its inverse is the finite geometric sum in its strictly upper triangular part. Row elimination removes the prefix-to-tail block, leaving its contractible identity-cone and the tail Roos cone. This proves the needed tail comparison without an unstated cofinality theorem.

source.place: Reduction to n≥m and the use of repleteness; Stacks Tags 0940–0941, 0947

proof.text: For $n\geq m$ form the $B_n$-complex $P_{n,m}=B_n\otimes_R K_m=[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell^m}B_n]$, augmented to $B_m$ by reduction in degree zero. Its fiber is $F_{n,m}=\operatorname{Cone}(P_{n,m}\to B_m)[-1]$. Directly, $H^0(P_{n,m})=B_m$ and $H^{-1}(P_{n,m})=\ell^{n-m}B_n\cong B_m$, with no other cohomology. The map $B_m[1]\to F_{n,m}$ induced by $x\mapsto\ell^{n-m}x$ into degree $-1$ is a quasi-isomorphism: the augmentation is surjective in degree zero, so its fiber has exactly that degree $-1$ kernel as its only cohomology. This map is $B_n$-linear. For $n'\geq n$ the transition on these copies of $B_m[1]$ is multiplication by $\ell^{n'-n}$, since reduction sends $\ell^{n'-m}x$ to $\ell^{n-m}(\ell^{n'-n}x)$. The calculation also covers $n=m$, when this map into $B_n$ is the identity.

source.place: The displayed coefficient tensor product, its fiber, and the powers-of-ell transitions; Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 3.5.4

proof.text: Tensor these fiber triangles over $B_n$ with $Q_n$. K-flatness preserves the displayed fiber quasi-isomorphisms: a cone of a quasi-isomorphism is acyclic, and its tensor remains acyclic by the K-flat definition. We obtain a triangle of strict $R$-towers on $n\geq m$, whose middle tower is $T_n=Q_n\otimes_R K_m$ and whose right tower is $S_n=Q_n\otimes_{B_n}B_m$. The identification of the middle term is the chain-level reassociation $q\otimes(b\otimes k)\mapsto bq\otimes k$, with the tensor differential's usual signs. The left tower is quasi-isomorphic to $S_n[1]$ with transition from $n'$ to $n$ equal to $\ell^{n'-n}$ times the ordinary transition. All these assertions hold for strict towers, since the coefficient maps just computed commute with every semilinear transition of $Q$. The current normalized-tower definition applies to the canonical maps over $B_n\to B_m$, with $1\leq m\leq n$. The map $S_n\to Q_m$ is the adjoint of the actual semilinear transition $Q_n\to Q_m$, given on tensors by $q\otimes b\mapsto b\,t_{n,m}(q)$. The compatible evaluation isomorphisms from step 2 identify this map with the defining reduction map $C_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m\to C_m$, so normalization makes it a quasi-isomorphism in $D(B_m)$. K-flat change of rings computes these very maps, not just an abstract isomorphism of their source and target. They form a strict map from $S$ to the constant tower $Q_m$, by the original transition cocycle.

source.place: Tensor the coefficient-fiber triangle and apply normalization; Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 3.5.4–3.5.5

proof.text: On the left tower the composite of any $m$ consecutive transitions is zero, because $\ell^m$ kills every $S_n$ termwise. Thus its derived limit is zero by the strict-tower limit statement. Equivalently its shift operator has $s^m=0$ and $1-s$ has inverse $1+s+\cdots+s^{m-1}$. Apply the exact strict-tower derived-limit functor to the triangle: $R\lim T_n\to R\lim S_n$ is an isomorphism. The strict levelwise quasi-isomorphism $S\to\operatorname{const}(Q_m)$ identifies the latter limit with $Q_m$. For clarity, a constant tower has this derived limit because the kernel of $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on $\prod_{n\geq m}Q_m$ is the diagonal $Q_m$, and this map is split surjective as a map of complexes: for $y=(y_n)$ set $x_m=0$ and $x_{m+r}=-\sum_{j=m}^{m+r-1}y_j$. Each coordinate uses a finite sum and satisfies $x_n-x_{n+1}=y_n$. The associated Roos cone is therefore quasi-isomorphic to the diagonal $Q_m$.

source.place: The nilpotent left tower has zero derived limit, giving the reduction formula; Stacks Tags 0940–0941

proof.text: The finite free complex $K_m$ commutes with the products and cones in the Roos model: in degree $r$ the tensor-product terms are the same two factors $\prod_n Q_n^r$ and $\prod_n Q_n^{r+1}$ on both sides; reorder the finite direct sums and use the tensor differential signs to identify the differentials. Consequently $C\otimes_R^L B_m\simeq R\lim_{n\geq m}T_n$. Here tensor with $K_m$ computes the underlying $R$-complex of the derived tensor with $B_m$: resolve $C$ by a K-flat complex; tensoring its quasi-isomorphism with $K_m$ preserves a quasi-isomorphism, and tensoring the resolution $K_m\to B_m$ with that K-flat complex also preserves a quasi-isomorphism. Composing with the preceding step gives an isomorphism of underlying $R$-complexes to $C_m$. This composition is induced by the $m$th projection from the limit and the coefficient augmentation, since the product/cone identifications, the tail elimination, and $S\to Q_m$ preserve those projections.

source.place: Reduction as a two-term cone commutes with Rlim; the natural reduction morphism

proof.text: Check the coefficient category and canonicity of this last morphism. On sheaves the ordinary tensor-restriction adjunction for $R\to B_m$ sends $f:M\to\operatorname{Res}N$ to $m\otimes b\mapsto b f(m)$, with inverse evaluation at $m\otimes1$. Restriction is exact, since it changes only the scalar action, so its derived functor is itself and is everywhere defined. Derived change of rings is everywhere defined by K-flat resolutions. The derived-adjoint-functors statement therefore supplies the derived tensor-restriction adjunction. Under it the $m$th limit projection corresponds to the canonical map $C\otimes_R^L B_m\to C_m$ in $D(B_m)$. Its restriction to $D(R)$ is the isomorphism just calculated. Restriction detects quasi-isomorphisms because the underlying cohomology sheaves of a cone do not change, so the map is an isomorphism in $D(B_m)$ itself. For $k\leq m$ the resolution map $K_m\to K_k$ is $(\ell^{m-k},1)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$. Together with the tower cocycle it verifies that these are the natural, quotient-compatible maps, rather than unrelated isomorphisms at each level.

source.place: The word natural in the conclusion; Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 3.5.5–3.5.7

proof.text: We prove completeness with the uniformizer convention of the integral category. Write $L_j=[R\xrightarrow{\pi^j}R]$ with transition $(\pi,1)$ from $j+1$ to $j$. For each fixed $n$, the complex $Q_n$ is termwise killed by $\pi^{en}$, since $\ell^n=u^n\pi^{en}$. On the tail $j\geq en$ the complex $Q_n\otimes_R L_j$ is $Q_n\oplus Q_n[1]$, with transition identity on the first summand and multiplication by $\pi$ on the shifted summand (up to the fixed tensor sign convention). The shifted tower has $en$-fold zero transitions and hence zero derived limit; the first tower is constant. The canonical map $Q_n\to R\lim_j(Q_n\otimes_R L_j)$ is the inclusion into the unshifted summand and is an isomorphism. This is natural in the strict $n$-tower; the cutoff $en$ is used only to check an individual row, not as a common cutoff for all $n$.

source.place: The claim that a limit of power-torsion complexes is derived complete; Bhatt–Scholze §3.5; Stacks Tag 099M

proof.text: The two sequential derived limits of the strict double tower $Q_n\otimes_R L_j$ commute here by an explicit Roos calculation. Expand each limit as a product-cone. Both iterated models have four Roos components, indexed by two degrees in $\{0,1\}$, with common products $\prod_n\prod_j(Q_n\otimes_R L_j)^r\cong\prod_j\prod_n(Q_n\otimes_R L_j)^r$. These product identifications follow from their universal property (both specify all $(n,j)$ coordinates). The two shift operators commute because $Q$'s transitions are $R$-linear. Swap the two Roos degrees with sign $(-1)^{pq}$ in bidegree $(p,q)$; the total differentials then agree, giving an isomorphism of the iterated cones. There are only four summands in each total degree, so no interchange of an infinite sum with a product is involved. Termwise products compute the derived products by exactness, as above. For each fixed $j$, the finite-free tensor/cone calculation of step 7 identifies $C\otimes_R L_j$ with $R\lim_n(Q_n\otimes_R L_j)$. Taking the other limit and using step 9 gives a canonical isomorphism $C\to R\lim_j(C\otimes_R L_j)$. This is the completion unit: each inclusion into the degree-zero Koszul term has been preserved in the double-cone identification. Constant-completion equivalence with $A=O,I=(\pi)$ identifies Koszul completion with quotient completion, respecting this unit. Thus $C$ and its canonical reduction maps fit the Roos triangle required by the definition of derived completeness.

source.place: Expand the completeness assertion using the Koszul completion unit; Stacks Tags 0940–0941, 099M; Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.5.2

proof.text: The same Roos triangle proves boundedness without any hypothesis on quasi-compactness of $T$. The common interval $[a,b]$ contains every $H^i(C_n)$ support. Since derived products commute with cohomology, both products in the triangle have cohomology only in $[a,b]$. The long exact sequence then gives $H^i(C)=0$ outside $[a,b+1]$. This is all the boundedness needed here; we do not assert an unjustified sharper endpoint. The needed consequence of repleteness is precisely the exactness of pro-etale countable module products already cited.

source.place: The sentence bounded since the pro-etale topos is replete; Stacks Tag 0947

proof.text: Finally fix any $j\geq1$ and choose $N$ with $eN\geq j$. The finite ring $D_j=O/\pi^j$ is a quotient of $O/\ell^N$. K-flat scalar associativity gives $C\otimes_R^L(D_j)_T\simeq(C\otimes_R^L B_N)\otimes_{B_N}^L(D_j)_T\simeq C_N\otimes_{B_N}^L(D_j)_T$. To see the first reassociation also for the completed coefficient ring, take a K-flat $R$-resolution $P$ of $C$: $P\otimes_R B_N$ is K-flat over $B_N$, because its tensor with an acyclic $B_N$-complex is $P$ tensored with that same acyclic complex restricted to $R$. Thus both sides are computed by the identical complex $P\otimes_R(D_j)_T$. Apply clause 2 of the current finite-coefficient scalar-extension statement to the unital quotient map $O/\ell^N\to D_j$ and the identity $D_j\to D_j$. Both rings are finite by step 1 and killed by $\ell^N$, since $eN\geq j$, and $C_N$ has constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in the common $[a,b]$ by the current normalized-tower definition. That clause gives constructible cohomology and Tor amplitude in the same $[a,b]$ after extension. It requires neither flatness nor finite projective dimension of $D_j$ over $O/\ell^N$. No Tate-twist clause or invertibility of $\ell$ on $T$ is used. Taking the module $(D_j)_T$ itself as the Tor-amplitude test shows that its cohomology is supported in $[a,b]$, independently of $j$. We have proved derived completeness and bounded constructibility for every uniformizer reduction, with one common support interval. These are exactly the conditions of the integral-category definition, so $C\in D^b_c(T,O)$. Together with step 8 this proves both conclusions of the item, retaining the original $\ell$-power natural maps.
